accuracy.evidence: Checked a.c./d.c. definitions, pd–time graph shapes, and UK mains ≈ 230 V at 50 Hz (US ≈ 120 V at 60 Hz) against AQA GCSE Physics Electricity. What reverses is pd/current, not the metal lattice.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets: battery called a.c.; swapping 230 V with 50 Hz; frequency treated as voltage; claiming nothing reverses; guessing from wire colour.

lab_distinct.evidence: flagacdc compares pd–time graphs and mains values. flagcirc teaches current/voltage in circuits; flagseries is series/parallel vocabulary. Under 30% shingle overlap expected.

lab_teaches.evidence: Learner reveals flat d.c. and waving a.c. graphs, recalls UK 230 V / 50 Hz, names what reverses, and orders graph-first identification.

predictions.evidence: Predictions offer battery→a.c., flat mains forever, 230 Hz, atoms reversing, and colour-guessing as tempting wrong options the lab disproves.

challenge_feedback.evidence: Feedback tags ac/dc/swap/bat/atom/miss/true name the slip: battery vs mains, swapped V/Hz, atoms vs pd.

readability.evidence: Uses precise terms: alternating current, direct current, potential difference, frequency, hertz, half-cycle. Short kid sentences.

no_filler.evidence: No filler. Kid paragraphs cover d.c., a.c., mains values, what reverses; adult lists mistakes and lab moves.

mobile.evidence: Graph drawings and option rows fit narrow canvases; button twins for every reveal.

accessibility.evidence: Buttons mirror taps; live aria-label; challenge group labelled; axe AA via pipeline walk.

sources: AQA GCSE Physics (8463) Electricity — direct and alternating potential difference; mains supply
UK statutory mains values: approximately 230 V at 50 Hz
